# Context Bench

> Empirical benchmark measuring how context building affects LLM-generated code. One model (Qwen 3.8 27B FP8 on vLLM) solves the same 30 coding tasks across 3 repository sizes (S, M, L) and 2,122 runs, varying only how context is assembled — from single-file and hand-picked-file baselines and whole-repository prompts to retrieval context builders (BM25 and embeddings), signature maps, minimal agentic harnesses (file-search and symbol-editing agents), and Antigravity as an external harness reference.

- Round: Prompt v4 round, results as of 26 November 2026
- Key findings (thinking on): Minimal agentic harnesses passed 92% (file-search agent) and 96% (symbol-reading, in-place-editing agent) overall (≥82% on every repo size), compared with 23% for the single-file baseline and 67% for the best retrieval context builder. Clean passes rose from 10% (single-file baseline) to 82% (symbol-editing agent). Helper reuse rose from 3% when unseen to 95% with full source in context.
- Author: Kiryl Dubarenka · License: MIT

## Pages

- [Results](https://context.engineeringthefuture.ai/): Experiment report for the Prompt v4 round (26 November 2026) — pass rates across single-file baselines, whole-repository prompts, retrieval context builders, signature maps, and minimal agentic harnesses, across repo sizes S/M/L, helper reuse, code quality penalties, thinking off vs on, and token cost.
- [Method](https://context.engineeringthefuture.ai/method): How context-bench measures the effect of context building with deliberately simple context builders, plus the levels, fair-comparison rules, labels, reuse, clean runs and blind grading.
- [Levels](https://context.engineeringthefuture.ai/levels): How context-bench builds the model's context across every strategy family — from single-file and whole-repository prompts to BM25/embedding retrieval, signature maps, and minimal tool-using agentic harnesses: what goes into the prompt, how retrieval ranks, and which tools the agents get.
- [Tasks](https://context.engineeringthefuture.ai/tasks): Every context-bench task with its text, the helpers it needs, decoys, hidden tests and reference solution.
- [Cases](https://context.engineeringthefuture.ai/cases): Single runs from the context-bench v4 round that show something the aggregate numbers hide: a helper reused without being seen, an agent caught by its own test, documentation drift, an ambiguous task, and an agent harness that ran empty commands.
- [Guide](https://context.engineeringthefuture.ai/guide): What it takes to run context-bench. Python and an OpenAI-compatible API are required, while an embedder, cache control and a judge are optional.
- [Raw data](https://context.engineeringthefuture.ai/data): Every run's prompt split into colour-coded parts, the model's thinking, answer or tool transcript, patch and test output.
- [Downloads](https://context.engineeringthefuture.ai/downloads): Raw results, grades and run bundles from context-bench, with versions pinned.

## Machine-Readable Data

- [Runs index (JSON)](https://context.engineeringthefuture.ai/raw/index.json): Metadata, outcomes, token counts, reuse flags, and judge scores for every published run.
- [Tasks catalog (JSON)](https://context.engineeringthefuture.ai/raw/tasks.json): All 30 tasks with prompts, target files, needed helpers, decoys, hidden tests, reference solutions, and difficulty ratings.
- [Per-run bundles](https://context.engineeringthefuture.ai/raw/runs/): Individual run JSON files (`https://context.engineeringthefuture.ai/raw/runs/<run_id>.json`) containing segmented prompts, reasoning, tool transcripts, patches, test output, and judge penalties.

## Optional

- [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/engineeringthefutureai/context-bench): Harness code, fixture repositories, task definitions, and grading scripts.
- [Experiment Design](https://github.com/engineeringthefutureai/context-bench/blob/main/docs/design.md): Architecture and task design notes.
- [Sitemap](https://context.engineeringthefuture.ai/sitemap.xml): XML sitemap of all indexable pages.
